newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Northwest hydropower restrictions seen easing.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Northwest hydropower restrictions seen easing.

text.p: Flow restrictions at hydropower dams in the Pacific Northwest will likely be lifted by the end of the day, Cindy Henriksen, chief of the Army Corps of Engineers' reservoir control center in Portland, Ore, said Monday.
Flows at the Grand Coulee dam in Washington on the Columbia River were restricted late last week amid concerns of downstream flooding from heavy rain.
"Over the weekend Coulee just passed inflows. We expect to remove those restrictions today," said Henriksen.

Flows at Grand Coulee have been just under 130 thousand cubic feet per second (kcfs), but the rate for the coming week will depend on inflows and Bonneville Power Administration (BPA) needs, she added.
The reservoir at John Day dam on the Columbia was drawn down late last week, also for flood control, but was allowed to refill over the weekend, Henriksen said.
John Day reservoir will be kept near current storage levels because of construction work, she added.
